nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Eco-friendly construction materials|Biodegradable and recyclable insulation_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the primary purpose of the study on bio-based insulation materials?
nodes.answer: The primary purpose is to provide comprehensive environmental information on bio-based thermal insulation materials to empower professionals in making informed decisions and promoting their selection.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract Purpose Bio-based insulation materials can have a significant impact in achieving net zero target in the construction sector. However, they face challenges due to lack of data on environmental performances and professional perception, hindering their proliferation. This study aims to combine scenario-based and dynamic analyses of environmental performances to provide comprehensive environmental information on bio-based thermal insulation materials. The goal is to empower professionals with robust information, facilitating informed decisions and promoting the selection of bio-based materials. Methods Data on manufacturing, use, recyclability, and technical performance of eleven commercially available natural insulation materials were collected from the literature to create a Life Cycle Inventory (LCI). For each material, a scenario- based life cycle assessment (LCA) was conducted by modelling variation in manufacturing, transportation, end-of-life and material properties, using the UK as the primary case study. Materials were compared to three non-bio-based insulation materials by ranking the thirteen environmental impact categories in EN 15804(2013) + A2(2019) to give an exhaustive overview of their potential benefits and burdens. Additionally, a dynamic LCIA was performed to implement in the analysis both short-and long-term emissions, exploring the impact of biogenic carbon.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Eco-friendly construction materials|Biodegradable and recyclable insulation_qna_004
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What materials were found to have the lowest environmental impact in the scenario analysis?
nodes.answer: Recycled cotton and hemp fibre insulation were found to have the lowest impact across all categories.
nodes.paragraph: Results The scenario analysis highlighted that recycled cotton and hemp fibre insulation have the lowest impact across all impact categories, attributed to their sustainable manufacturing processes and minimal impacts at the end-of-life stage. The dynamic LCIA demonstrated that recycled textile insulation has the lowest impact both in the short-term (prior to waste disposal) and the long-term (post-waste disposal), regardless of the chosen end-of-life scenario. Furthermore, it indicated that cotton and hemp fibre have a negligible impact on global temperature changes, achieving a net-zero effect in the short- term and close-to-zero impact in the long-term. Conclusion The novelty of this paper lies in its comprehensive investigation of the environmental impacts of bio-based ther - mal insulation materials, employing multiple tools to enhance generalizability. These results will support decision-making by providing data ranges to help practitioners identify the most environmentally friendly insulation materials. Additionally, they offer insights into how similar products compare within that range, driving progress in the built environment towards net-zero emissions. Whilst the full dataset and evaluation methods are illustrated through a UK-based case study, this method can be adapted for specific scenarios and projects, due to the transparency of data and methods.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Eco-friendly construction materials|Biodegradable and recyclable insulation_qna_006
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What are the main advantages of bio-based insulation materials compared to traditional fossil-based insulations?
nodes.answer: Bio-based insulation materials use renewable resources, can store carbon when produced under environment-friendly practices, and, if not recyclable, can sometimes be used for soil conditioning.
nodes.paragraph: Standard construction practices are still reliant on products made from fossil-based resources, especially for insulation materials. Insulation materials manufactured from bio-based resources have emerged as an alternative to the more tradi- tional fossil-based insulations. Bio-based insulations have the advantage of using renewable resources, if produced under environment-friendly practices, can store carbon (Lawrence et al. 2013) and, if not recyclable, can sometimes be used for soil conditioning (Beigbeder et al. 2019). Several studies have found lower environmental impacts for some bio-based material (Schmidt et al. 2004a; Murphy and Norton 2008; Pargana et al. 2014; Schulte et al. 2021; Carcassi et al. 2022). Schmidt et al. (2004a, b) and Schulte et al. (2021) compared the environmental impact of plant- based insulation materials to conventional materials. Both Schmidt et al. (2004a, b) and Schulte et al. (2021) performed a cradle-to-grave life cycle assessment (LCA) and compared the materials using thermal resistance as the functional unit. Products were compared by investigating all the environ- mental impacts prescribed in International Standard Organi- zation (1997).

nodes.answer: The main focus of the studies is to investigate the environmental impacts of novel bio-based insulation materials using Global Warming Potential (GWP100) as the primary indicator.

nodes.question: What was the focus of the studies by Carcassi et al. (2022) and Hawkins et al. (2021)?
nodes.answer: The focus of the studies was to demonstrate the significant potential of bio-based insulation to offset carbon emissions and highlight the advantages of bio-based materials based on specific products.
nodes.paragraph: The dynamic LCIA in Carcassi et al. ( 2022 ) and Hawkins et al. ( 2021 ) demonstrated the significant potential of bio-based insulation to offset carbon emissions. Whilst both Carcassi et al. (2022) and Hawk - ins et al. (2021) demonstrated the advantages of bio-based materials, they based their work on specific products, using EPDs for Hawkins et al. (2021) and developing a Life Cycle Inventory (LCI) for a small-scale material production in Carcassi et al. (2022). Their investigation is therefore lim- ited to specific contexts. In this study the investigation of the environmental impacts is based on a case study in which the construction site is based in the UK, but it not limited to specific manu- facturer locations, and products. Product variations (density and thermal conductivity) were considered in the LCA of eleven newly commercially available bio-based insulation materials. Data on manufacturing, transportation, current and potential practise for disposal were collected from 603 The International Journal of Life Cycle Assessment (2025) 30:601 620 literature to build LCIs for the studied materials.

nodes.question: How can wool fibres be repurposed in industries?
nodes.answer: Wool fibres can be repurposed in industries for thermal and acoustic insulation purposes, as well as in pads for soaking up oil spills, showcasing the versatility and sustainability of wool in various applications.
